Conclusion of Rheology and Microscopy Studies Coatings were cast onto Mylar from the ASL, AFL and GDC slurries, using the doctor blade method. Rheology experiments were used to evaluate the effect that solid loading has on processability of the slurries. Microscopy was used to determine the quality of the dried coating and to investigate surface defects that may be present in order to support optimizing EEA manufacture. Achieving a stable coating parameter window in slot-die coating is not fully understood for non-Newtonian fluids. Furthermore, high coating speeds and a high-quality product are paramount for economically manufacturing the EEA. 2.4 Q4: Multi-layer coating has been made in this quarter: • Fabricated multilayer coatings of AFL/ASL, ASL/ASL and AFL/ASL/ASL • Fabricated varying thickness of ASL/ASL via slot-die coating (100-600 μm) • Partial EEA with minimal ASL thickness (300 μm) was fabricated. Substantial progress was made in the slot-die coating of sequential layers of the EEA. The 2-layer ASL/ASL and AFL/ASL and 3-layer AFL/ASL/ASL coatings were successfully fabricated (Figure 18). Good control has been established for managing the gap height required for the individual layer thicknesses. In addition, various thicknesses of the ASL layers were coated, with controlled thicknesses between 100 and 600 μm for the 2-layer ASL/ASL, with a minimal ASL thickness of ~300 μm used to coat a partial EEA including the AFL, without the final GDC layer. 12 Figure 18 SEM micrographs of (A) AFL coated onto thin, single layer ASL, (B&C) AFL coated onto 2- layer ASL, showing good contact and homogeneous morphology at interface. Silicone coated Mylar which had previously been determined to be of interest for milestones involving lamination and slot-die coating, has been utilized and tested. This substrate demonstrated the desired “peelability” of the coatings, proving far superior when compared to the uncoated substrate used in previous work. Further evaluation of the ASL utilized SEM for the fabricated 2- and 3- layer samples, demonstrating good interface and morphology between the sequentially coated layers (Figure 19).
